guide.title: Millinocket Ski Slope: a rope tow rebuilt, debuting February 27, 2026
guide.intro: A portable rope tow for beginner skiers was first set up by the Millinocket Recreation Committee near the town athletic field and Hillcrest Golf Club circa the winter of 1951-52, per New England Ski History's Millinocket page, expanding by 1953 to include a toboggan run and lighting. In September 2022, per the same source, Millinocket Town Manager Peter Jamieson announced intentions to "bring the ski tow back to life," beginning a multi-year revival effort.

sections.heading: A grant-funded rebuild
sections.body: Per Maine WinterKids' "Town of Millinocket Parks & Rec" community-highlights page (published July 5, 2024; last modified September 4, 2025), a $10,000 Downhill 24 Outdoor Fund grant was used by the Millinocket Parks and Recreation department to "purchase a rope tow, revitalize the Millinocket Ski Tow," covering trail cleanup, an electrical installation, and a heated warming hut. By September 2023, per New England Ski History, the project had also secured $22,500 each from the American Rescue Plan Act and from Katahdin Area Trails, with construction accelerating in August 2024.

sections.heading: The February 2026 debut
sections.body: The rebuilt rope tow debuted Friday, February 27, 2026, per New England Ski History's year-by-year table, corroborated by Unofficial Networks, which reported "On Friday, the Town of Millinocket opened up its new rope tow" — framing the debut as "Maine's first new ski area opening since 2022." For its opening weekend, per the same report, the rope tow ran Friday 3:00-5:00 p.m. and Saturday-Sunday 1:00-5:30 p.m. The Town of Millinocket's own Recreation Department page describes "a sliding hill with a rope tow all in the Recreation complex," located at 199 State Street adjacent to Stearns High School.

sections.heading: Status beyond the debut
sections.body: Whether the rope tow runs again for the 2026-27 season is undetermined. As of this writing, the Town of Millinocket's homepage, its Recreation Department page, the Recreation Advisory Committee's posted minutes, the Katahdin Area Trails website, and New England Ski History's own year-by-year table — whose most recent entry is the February 27, 2026 debut — carry no 2026-27 schedule, price, or announcement.

sections.heading: In Millinocket
sections.body: The Millinocket Historical Society, established in 1979 by residents Polly and Bud Segee, collects and preserves the town's history and artifacts and is open Thursday, Friday and Saturday from noon to 3 p.m., per the town's own website. The Boreal Theater is a 48-seat black-box community theater and registered 501(c)(3) nonprofit that its own site describes as functioning as "a community meeting space, education & healing space for groups & individuals, art gallery, rental space for events." The Antique Snowmobile Museum, adjacent to the Northern Timber Cruisers snowmobile club's clubhouse, describes itself on its own site as holding "the largest collection of antique snowmobiles in the northeast," including models tested locally by curator Steve Campbell's father, Earlan B. Campbell, who "was instrumental in working with the early Polaris prototypes."

faq.question: When did the rebuilt Millinocket rope tow open?
faq.answer: Friday, February 27, 2026, per New England Ski History and Unofficial Networks, following a town-led revival effort that began with a September 2022 announcement from Town Manager Peter Jamieson.

faq.question: Is the Millinocket Ski Slope running this season?
faq.answer: No source establishes a 2026-27 schedule. The town's own website, Recreation Department page, Recreation Advisory Committee minutes, and New England Ski History's year-by-year table all lack any 2026-27 entry as of this writing.

places.name: Antique Snowmobile Museum
places.address: 10 Northern Cruise Trail, Lake Road, Millinocket, ME 04462
places.summary: A museum of vintage snowmobiles beside the Northern Timber Cruisers clubhouse, tracing local Polaris prototype testing.
places.history: The Antique Snowmobile Museum, adjacent to the Northern Timber Cruisers snowmobile club's clubhouse, describes itself on its own site as holding "the largest collection of antique snowmobiles in the northeast," including Polaris, Arctic Cat, Yamaha and Ski-Doo models. Curator Steve Campbell follows his father, Earlan B. Campbell, who the site says "was instrumental in working with the early Polaris prototypes," much of that testing having occurred locally in the Millinocket and Allagash region.
